dialogue.user: Thank you for the recommendations! I'm particularly interested in the **Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes** because they seem to fit my preferences well. Could you tell me more about the reviews? What do customers generally like and dislike about these shoes?
dialogue.agent:
Here are the top reviews for the **Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Gore-TEX Trail Running Shoes** that customers have found most helpful:

1. **Rating: 5.0**
   - **Title:** DAY 1 COMFORT
   - **Review:** I got these for my dad. He’s a big guy, and I’m trying to get him to exercise. We ordered him the same size he wears for all others shoes, so the size is true fit (11.5). We went walking 2 miles this morning. He says they’re the most comfortable shoes he’s ever worn; no feet pain, no back pain. He didn’t complain once while walking. He’s got flat feet, so normally his feet hurt if we walk a lot (like around the mall for 2 hours). He recommends these shoes for big guys with flat feet starting to exercise again. Day 1 Comfort! Get them.

2. **Rating: 5.0**
   - **Title:** Longtime fan of Salomon
   - **Review:** I've been a fan of Salomon's shoes for a long time. As a former Special Operations Soldier, I needed shoes that could stand up to harsh field conditions while still being comfortable. I used to wear an earlier model of these shoes before switching to the Speedcross, and while I liked the Speedcross, I've come back to the Pro 3D because these shoes are more well-rounded for a wider variety of terrain and conditions. They also have a wider toe box that accommodates my need for a little more space due to two separate foot surgeries. I am particularly fond of the GTX (Goretex) lining because it allows for a low level of waterproofing without causing my feet to overheat (read: sweat and stink), and it helps to keep the sand from permeating the shoe. When paired with Salomon trail gaiters, I rarely have any debris or sand in my shoes after long hikes, trail runs, or trailjoring with my dog. Although I am a female, I tend to prefer the darker, more subdued colors of the men's line of shoes to the bright neon colors available in the women's line.

3. **Rating: 5.0**
   - **Title:** Awesome grip!
   - **Review:** Finally got to take these out today for a 5 mile run. I bought them for exactly what today’s conditions threw at me: slushy streets, icy side walks, crunchy snow covered trails, and wintry mix stuff falling from the sky. My feet stayed dried and locked in. The laces stayed tight, and I could adjust them on the fly with gloves on. The soles gripped whatever it could, and mitigated whatever slippage occurred whenever it could not. I bought these sneakers because I have a boot by salomon with the same sole, and I liked how well they performed. Great shoe!

Would you like more information or assistance with anything else?

Thank you for the additional options! The **Kenetrek Desert Guide Non-Insulated Hiking Boot** seems interesting, but I noticed it doesn't have a waterproof membrane. Since waterproofing is important to me, I think I'll pass on this one.

The **Lowa Men's Renegade GTX Mid Hiking Boot** looks promising. Could you share some of the top reviews for these boots? I'm particularly interested in what customers have to say about their comfort and durability.
dialogue.agent:
Here are the top reviews for the **Lowa Men's Renegade GTX Mid Hiking Boot** that customers have found most helpful:

1. **Rating: 1.0**
   - **Title:** Another Case of Sole De-lamination-SOL Warranty
   - **Review:** These Lowa boots have had the same sole separation others here have experienced. These boots have very little wear on them, and have self-destructed. 90% of this failure happened on one 4 hour outing, and it was getting to the point that the sole was about to fall off. I would have had to pull the soles off in order to walk without tripping on them had I any farther to go. Lowa says this is not warrant-able, and is a normal occurrence with the material they use. I feel that if the boots have a “shelf life” where they fall apart without much use, they should come with a warning to that effect. I'm done with Lowa, and am buying quality USA made boots instead of Chinese made from now on. Sad, but Vasque and others have gone the same way. I have had many pairs of boots over the past 50 years, and none have done this.

2. **Rating: 5.0**
   - **Title:** Comfortable and sturdy hiking boot.
   - **Review:** I'm out 2 to 4 times a week birding and trail mountain climbing. Depending on terrain, weather, and miles I'll wear Solomon Gortex trail shoes or Keen Targhee lightweight hiking boots. It was raining the last time I wore my Keens (two years old) and my feet got soaking wet and cold. I decided I had had it with sock type hiking boots and ordered the Lowa Renegade II GTX boots from Amazon, based primarily on waterproof, all-leather, and lightweight characteristics. I was worried about some of the comments about the boot being too narrow. When I put them on, wow, what a comfortable fit! With no breaking in, I wore them on a 6-mile hike up and back a mountain, and everything was perfect - no rubbing, no slipping going downhill, great traction, great support on rough terrain. These boots are so good, I now wear them on easy hikes, where previously, I used my Solomon trail shoes. Note: not appropriate for backpacking over rough trail or mountaineering.

3. **Rating: 1.0**
   - **Title:** 100-mile boot...$200 mistake
   - **Review:** I purchased this pair of Lowa Renegades for my husband. They are come in a wide size which is great because his wide feet don't fit into any other boots, and he says they are comfortable. I can't think of anything else good to say about them. This seemingly comfortable boot is plagued by poor quality and durability. The rubber at the front of the boot started separating from the leather at less than 100 miles of use. It is cracking, crumbling, peeling, and it looks like the whole thing may detach with a little bit more use. The pictures are after our last hike, at approximately 125 miles in 8 months of use. My husband doesn't like hiking, so it's not like he is some bushwhacking pioneer exploring the rugged backcountry. We only hike on established trails (some on rocky terrain), and he used these boots for day hiking and a few overnight trips (with relatively light ~20lb pack). Apparently this rugged "all-terrain" boot can't handle that. I expected much more mileage out of a $225 pair of boots. I contacted Lowa regarding the warranty, and they asked me to send it to them for inspection. Without a guarantee that it would be covered by warranty, I didn't want to waste the money shipping it to them, so I returned them to REI where I got them. Based on this experience, I can only conclude that these boots are meant for hikes on flat, dirt trails with little to no rock...basically trails you can walk with a pair of flip flops. If you can do without the ankle support, I recommend you ditch these boots for a pair of trail runners - 1/3 the price, much lighter, and will last you longer than this piece of junk.

Would you like more information or assistance with anything else?

top_reviews.title: DAY 1 COMFORT
top_reviews.text:
I got these for my dad. He’s a big guy, and I’m trying to get him to exercise.
We ordered him the same size he wears for all others shoes, so the size is true fit (11.5).
We went walking 2 miles this morning.
He says they’re the most comfortable shoes he’s ever worn; no feet pain, no back pain.
He didn’t complain once while walking.
He’s got flat feet, so normally his feet hurt if we walk a lot (like around the mall for 2 hours).
He recommends these shoes for big guys with flat feet starting to exercise again.
Day 1 Comfort!
Get them.

top_reviews.title: Longtime fan of Salomon
top_reviews.text:
I've been a fan of Salomon's shoes for a long time. As a former Special Operations Soldier, I needed shoes that could stand up to harsh field conditions while still being comfortable. I used to wear an earlier model of these shoes before switching to the Speedcross, and while I liked the Speedcross, I've come back to the Pro 3D because these shoes are more well-rounded for a wider variety of terrain and conditions. They also have a wider toe box that accommodates my need for a little more space due to two separate foot surgeries.

I am particularly fond of the GTX (Goretex) lining because it allows for a low level of waterproofing without causing my feet to overheat (read: sweat and stink), and it helps to keep the sand from permeating the shoe. When paired with Salomon trail gaiters, I rarely have any debris or sand in my shoes after long hikes, trail runs, or trailjoring with my dog.

Although I am a female, I tend to prefer the darker, more subdued colors of the men's line of shoes to the bright neon colors available in the women's line.

top_reviews.title: Awesome grip!
top_reviews.text:
Finally got to take these out today for a 5 mile run. I bought them for exactly what today’s conditions threw at me: slushy streets, icy side walks, crunchy snow covered trails, and wintry mix stuff falling from the sky.

My feet stayed dried and locked in. The laces stayed tight, and I could adjust them on the fly with gloves on. The soles gripped whatever it could, and mitigated whatever slippage occurred whenever it could not.

I bought these sneakers because I have a boot by salomon with the same sole, and I liked how well they performed.

Great shoe!

top_reviews.title: Another Case of Sole De-lamination-SOL Warranty
top_reviews.text: These Lowa boots have had the same sole separation others here have experienced. These boots have very little wear on them, and have self-destructed. 90% of this failure happened on one 4 hour outing, and it was getting to the point that the sole was about to fall off. I would have had to pull the soles off in order to walk without tripping on them had I any farther to go. Lowa says this is not warrant-able, and is a normal occurrence with the material they use. I feel that if the boots have a “shelf life” where they fall apart without much use, they should come with a warning to that effect. I'm done with Lowa, and am buying quality USA made boots instead of Chinese made from now on. Sad, but Vasque and others have gone the same way. I have had many pairs of boots over the past 50 years, and none have done this.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable and sturdy hiking boot.
top_reviews.text: I'm out 2 to 4 times a week birding and trail mountain climbing.  Depending on terrain, weather, and miles I'll wear Solomon Gortex trail shoes or Keen Targhee lightweight hiking boots.  It was raining the last time I wore my Keens (two years old) and my feet got soaking wet and cold.  I decided I had had it with sock type hiking boots and ordered the Lowa Renegade II GTX boots from Amazon, based primarily on waterproof, all-leather, and lightweight characteristics. I was worried about some of the comments about the boot being too narrow.  When I put them on, wow, what a comfortable fit!  With no breaking in, I wore them on a 6-mile hike up and back a mountain, and everything was perfect - no rubbing, no slipping going downhill, great traction, great support on rough terrain.  These boots are so good, I now wear them on easy hikes, where previously, I used my Solomon trail shoes.  Note: not appropriate for backpacking over rough trail or mountaineering.

top_reviews.title: 100-mile boot...$200 mistake
top_reviews.text:
I purchased this pair of Lowa Renegades for my husband. They are come in a wide size which is great because his wide feet don't fit into any other boots, and he says they are comfortable. I can't think of anything else good to say about them.

This seemingly comfortable boot is plagued by poor quality and durability. The rubber at the front of the boot started separating from the leather at less than 100 miles of use. It is cracking, crumbling, peeling, and it looks like the whole thing may detach with a little bit more use. The pictures are after our last hike, at approximately 125 miles in 8 months of use. My husband doesn't like hiking, so it's not like he is some bushwhacking pioneer exploring the rugged backcountry. We only hike on established trails (some on rocky terrain), and he used these boots for day hiking and a few overnight trips (with relatively light ~20lb pack). Apparently this rugged "all-terrain" boot can't handle that. I expected much more mileage out of a $225 pair of boots.

I contacted Lowa regarding the warranty, and they asked me to send it to them for inspection. Without a guarantee that it would be covered by warranty, I didn't want to waste the money shipping it to them, so I returned them to REI where I got them.

Based on this experience, I can only conclude that these boots are meant for hikes on flat, dirt trails with little to no rock...basically trails you can walk with a pair of flip flops. If you can do without the ankle support, I recommend you ditch these boots for a pair of trail runners - 1/3 the price, much lighter, and will last you longer than this piece of junk.
